text:
4.1 Statement Ideology based on WVS


Code
load("parquet/PCAall.Rdata")
sttmts <- read_parquet("sttmts.parquet")


A principal component analysis of the 100 statements based on the responses of all respondents of the World Value Survey 2018 with complete data (N = 33926) shows a clear left-right ideological dimension. The first principal component (PC1) explains 13.5% of the variance in the data and is highly correlated with the left-right self-placement of respondents (r = 0.82). The statements can be ordered along this dimension, and we can classify them as progressive or conservative based on their position on PC1.


Code
gg <- sttmts |>
  arrange(desc(WVS_PC1)) |>
  mutate(Worldview_Statement_fct = fct_inorder(Worldview_Statement)) |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = WVS_PC1,
    y = Worldview_Statement_fct,
    color = worldview,
    fill = WVS_PC1,
    tooltip = Worldview_Statement
  )) +
  geom_col_interactive() +
  labs(x = "", y = "", color = "Ideology LLM coded", fill = "WVS PC1") +
  scale_fill_continuous(palette = "RdYlBu", limits = c(-1, 1)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("blue", "red")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 8) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank())
girafe(ggobj = gg, options = list(opts_toolbar(position = "top", fixed = TRUE)))

4.3 Number of surviving statements per run


Code
max_width <- 0.9 # total width available per category slot
step_max <- 0.18 # never space wider than this

gb_data <- bubbles_summary |>
  pivot_longer(
    c(num_statements, num_shared40_statements),
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "num"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    variable = fct_recode(
      variable,
      "#statements shared by >40 agents" = "num_shared40_statements",
      "#statements" = "num_statements"
    ) |>
      fct_rev(),
    onclick = paste0(
      'window.open("networkexplorer.html?net=',
      run_id_desc,
      '_t100")'
    ),
    xcat = interaction(openmindedness, post),
    x_num = as.numeric(xcat)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    n_tied = n(),
    step = pmin(step_max, max_width / pmax(n_tied - 1, 1)),
    x_pos = x_num + (row_number() - (n_tied + 1) / 2) * step,
    .by = c(M, variable, xcat, num)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    xcat = fct_recode(
      xcat,
      "Feed\nOp. 1" = "1.F",
      "Feed\nOp. 3" = "3.F",
      "Both\nOp. 1" = "1.FS",
      "Both\nOp. 3" = "3.FS",
      "Social\nOp. 1" = "1.S",
      "Social\nOp. 3" = "3.S"
    ),
    M = fct_recode(
      factor(M),
      "5 Statements per agent" = "5",
      "10 Statements per agent" = "10"
    )
  )

gb <- gb_data |>
  ggplot(
    aes(
      x = x_pos,
      y = num,
      fill = post,
      shape = variable,
      alpha = variable,
      tooltip = run_id_desc,
      onclick = onclick,
      data_id = run_id_desc
    )
  ) +
  geom_point_interactive(size = 1.6, stroke = 0.3) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq_along(levels(gb_data$xcat)),
    labels = levels(gb_data$xcat),
    minor_breaks = NULL
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(minor_breaks = seq(0, 66, 2), breaks = seq(0, 66, 10)) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(21, 22)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("red", "green", "blue")) +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c(1, 0.5)) +
  #facet_wrap(~M) +
  facet_grid(variable ~ M, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Posting and Openmindedness",
    y = "",
    shape = "",
    fill = "Posting"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  guides(alpha = "none", fill = "none", shape = "none") +
  theme(
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )
girafe(
  ggobj = gb,
  options = list(
    opts_toolbar(position = "top", fixed = TRUE)
  )
)

text:
6.2 Eye-balled network types
Before turning to a mathematical network metrics to quantify different types we made a manual coding using eye-bulling on three different aspects: number of bubbles quantifies if the network is better quantified to be 1, 2, or 3 bubbles. A bubble is similar to what is also called a module or a cluster. It is supposed to be a group of nodes which are more connected among each other than to the other nodes. In our manual coding a we consider a diverse network without a clear bubble structure to be one bubble. As this classification can not distinguish between tightly connected bubbles and wide stread structures, the next aspect is bubbleness. Bubbleness has a value of 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, or 1 where 1 means that all bubbles have not many statements and are therefore tightly connected and 0 means that the number of statements is still very large and bubble structure if not visible. Finally, parity takes also the values 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, or 1. A network with one bubble always receives the value 0. For networks with two or three bubbles 1 specifies that the bubbles are almost equal in size with respect to the number of agents, while 0 stands for a network where one of the bubbles includes almost all nodes.
So, the clearest indicator of a consensusal society is with one bubble with maximal bubbleness (1, 1, 0). A maximally bipolarized polarized soceity has two bubbles with maximal bubbleness and parity. is most clearly quantified with (2, 1, 1).


Code
statements_count <- memory |>
  filter(t == 100) |>
  count(run_id, S_id) |>
  summarize(
    num_statements = n(),
    num_shared5_statements = sum(n >= 5),
    num_shared30_statements = sum(n >= 30),
    num_shared50_statements = sum(n >= 50),
    num_shared70_statements = sum(n >= 70),
    .by = run_id
  )

runs_analysis <- runs_core |>
  left_join(
    runs_annotations |> select(run_id, num_bub, bubbleness, parity),
    by = join_by(run_id)
  ) |>
  left_join(statements_count, by = join_by(run_id)) |>
  select(
    M,
    Openminded = openmindedness,
    Posting = post,
    Seed = seed,
    num_statements,
    num_shared5_statements,
    num_shared30_statements,
    num_shared50_statements,
    num_shared70_statements,
    Number_Bubbles = num_bub,
    Bubbleness = bubbleness,
    Parity = parity,
    Filename = run_id_desc
  )
runs_analysis |>
  gt() |>
  opt_interactive(
    use_sorting = TRUE,
    use_filters = TRUE,
    use_highlight = TRUE,
    use_compact_mode = TRUE,
    use_text_wrapping = TRUE,
    use_page_size_select = TRUE,
    page_size_default = 10,
    page_size_values = c(10, 25, 72),
    pagination_type = c("numbers", "jump", "simple")
  ) |>
  cols_width(
    M ~ px(60),
    Openminded ~ px(120),
    Posting ~ px(90),
    Seed ~ px(90),
    Number_Bubbles ~ px(140),
    Bubbleness ~ px(100),
    Parity ~ px(90),
    Filename ~ px(500)
  )
